newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Knife edge electoral count for WA upper house.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Knife edge electoral count for WA upper house.

text.p: The 103-year conservative control of Western Australia's upper house -- the Legislative Council -- appears to have been all-but broken following Saturday's state election.

While the Liberal Party/National Party coalition was the clear winner in the Legislative Assembly, even Liberal insiders were saying today the most likely scenario in the Council is an even split between Government and non-government members.
If the coalition has to provide a President, it will be left in a minority on the Council floor. (Unlike the Senate, the President of the Legislative Council has only a casting vote.)

Meanwhile, Labor Relations Minister, Graham Kierath, said he would challenge Resources Minister Colin Barnett for the deputy leadership of the Liberal Party when members hold their first post-election party meeting on Monday.
The coalition went into Saturday's election with 18 Council members compared to Labor's 14, one Green and one Independent.

With more than 50 per cent of the Council vote counted the coalition appears to have won 17 seats, Labor 12, the Greens 3, and the Australian Democrats two, including the seat previously held by the Independent.
In the 57-seat Legislative Assembly, and subject to two re-counts, the Liberals have won 29 seats (26 previously), Labor 19 (22), the Nationals 6 (6) and independents 3 (3).

The Clerk of the Council, Laurie Marguet, was quoted in The West Australian newspaper today as saying there was no provision in the WA Constitution to cover an even split of members but said the Council could not sit without a president.
When contacted by Reuters, spokespersons for the Greens, the Democrats and Labor all rejected any suggestion they would provide a candidate for the position.
